To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the formation of a ruthenium-vinyldene (Ru-C═C-R) interfacia bonding linkage was confirmed for the first time in stable ruthenium nanoparticles, and (2) the resulting nanoparticles could be functionalized with imine and vinyl-terminated molecules to give a new class of metal-ligand complexes with a unique heterocyclic structure at the metal-lignad interface.

(1) the self-assembly process of alkyne ligands onto the surface of ruthenium nanoparticles leads to the formation of Ru-vinylidenes, which can be further functionalized by imine and olefin metathesi reactions, and (2) the self- assembly process of alkyde ligands onto the ruthenium nanoparticles surface leads to the formation a Ru-carbyne, which cannot be further modified.

alkyne-functionalized metal nanoparticles have been synthesized and that the nature of the metal-ligands bonds formed at the metal-lagand interface depends on the electronic properties of the metal nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of a new class of alkyne-functionalized Ru nanoparticles, in which the metal-ligands are linked by a vinylidene bond, and the reactivity of these novel species in a variety of chemical transformations.
the synthesis and characterization of new ruthenium nanoparticles stabilized by the self-organization of 1-dodcycne onto the "naked" metal surface.
a new type of metal-ligand bond at the metal surface and its application in the synthesis of functionalized nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interfacial metal-ligand bonding in ruthenium nanoparticles is a dynamic process and is dependent on the ligands used to prepare the nanoparticles.
the formation of a stable Ru-vinylidenyl linkage at the metal-lagand interface is a key feature of the alkyne-functionalized Ru nanoparticles.
the Ru-vinylide bond was formed in the case of alkyne-stabilized ruthnium nanoparticles and the Ru-C≡ d π bond was formed in alkynide-stabilzed nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal-ligands bonds at the metal surface can be readily manipulated by changing the surface ligand.

the interfacial bonding of the alkyne-functionalized nanoparticles can be tuned by adjusting the acidity/basicity of the ligand, and the interfacial bond formation could be used to control the surface reactivity of the metal nanoparticles.
the metal-ligands interactions in these nanoparticles can be tuned by the choice of the stabilizing ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nature of the interfacial metal-ligand bonding linkage in the nanoparticles is highly dependent on the electronic properties and the nature of the functional groups in the stabilizing ligands.
the metal-ligands interface of metal nanoparticles can be functionalized by the formation of covalent bonds, and that these bonds are not limited to those with the metal core.
alkyne-functionalized nanoparticles are not necessarily stabilized via a Ru-C≡ bond at the metal surface but may also involve a Ru-vinylene (or vinylidene) linkage.
